# Draft:6th General Assembly of Prince Edward Island

}}
The 5th General Assembly of the Island of St. John  began in 1790 and lasted until 1802. It was marked by the stabilization of colonial governance under Lieutenant Governor Edmund Fanning and the formalization of the colony's legal records.
The Assembly sat at the pleasure of the Governor of St. John's Island, Edmund Fanning (colonial administrator).
Following the chaotic "dual governor" period of 1787, Lieutenant Governor Edmund Fanning solidified his authority during this assembly. His focus remained on resolving the "Land Question," specifically the collection of quit rents from absentee landlords and the management of land grants for Loyalists.
Late in this assembly's tenure (1798), the colony's name was officially changed from St. John's Island to Prince Edward Island to avoid confusion with other locations in the Atlantic, such as St. John's, Newfoundland.
Alexander Fletcher was chosen as speaker in 1790, Joseph Robinson from 1790-1794, and John Stewart from 1795-1801.
